source_claims.statement: Client-side analysis and endpoint scouting. Login page variables not controllable from query. /global-protect/getconfig.esp initially unpromising (static content). Initial SVG payloads failed in XML context.
Created lists of parameters and probes. SVG with proper namespace worked. Variant analysis found additional parameters and /ssl-vpn/getconfig.esp.

research_questions.formulation: After standard XSS fails on login and an endpoint looks static, do XML-returning configuration endpoints reflect parameters in a context that allows namespaced SVG or XHTML?
research_questions.anchor: pivot to parameter lists and namespace-aware payloads after initial failures
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether XML reflection can be made executable
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that static-looking or XML endpoints are safe from XSS

environment_model_updates: Parameters such as portal-prelogonuserauthcookie are reflected
Namespaces affect XML parsing and browser rendering

systematic_vs_exploratory.systematic: client-side review, parameter and probe list creation, variant analysis after first hit
systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: trying namespaced SVG after plain SVG failed in XML

negative_inconclusive: Login page: variables not controllable from query
Plain SVG: failed due to XML parsing rules
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat static-looking response as proof of no reflection
Namespace was required for the XML context
next_evidence_actions: Note CVE-2025-0133 and post-mitigation bypass re-test
layer_b_candidate_principles: When an endpoint returns XML, test whether reflected parameters can be turned into executable content via proper SVG/XHTML namespaces
After a first hit, variant analysis across parameters and related endpoints is high-value
model_vs_harness: Knowing GlobalProtect endpoints and XML namespace tricks is model knowledge; systematic parameter probing and variant checking can be harness.
